articles.title: Check the firm before you invest, FCA warns, as AI scams rise
articles.summary: A third (33%) of UK adults say they have seen an investment promotion in the past year that they believe used artificial intelligence (AI), new research from the FCA shows. Reports of investment fraud to Report Fraud that mention suspected use of AI have risen by nearly 400% in a year, up from 193 in 2024/25 to 956 in 2025/26. Investment fraud victims lost an average of £28,188 in 2025/26.Most people feel confident they could spot an AI investment scam, but that confidence is lower when a well-known person is involved. Almost two-thirds (62%) of adults say they could identify an investment scam that used AI. But less than half (49%) think they could tell whether a video or voice recording of a well-known person had been generated or altered by AI.Martin Lewis was the person most often named by those who thought they had seen a fake promotion featuring a well-known person.Under-35s are the most confident and the most exposed.
